_doc: Golden fixture from fixtures/reference-tours/01-place-des-vosges.md, loaded by scripts/human_reference_tours.py (composed 2026-04-26). Resolved against live Paris Neo4j 2026-04-29.
_resolution_method: Tag -> beat resolution re-runs the fixture's own script_body method against data/paris/beats.json, exact-first: (1) the tag name is the tail of exactly one corpus beat_id; (2) the quoted paragraph is a verbatim prefix of exactly one beat's script_body (not used for paragraphs carrying more than one tag, where the prose blends beats); (3) the machine-similarity resolution recovered from git 4ea26683, only where it names an existing beat and the two recovered runs agree. Ids are the durable corpus slugs (b.beat_id / stable_beat_id), never the per-database UUIDs minted at upload. Anything still unresolved is listed in unresolved_tags for human review and is deliberately absent from expected_stable_beat_ids.

notes: Round-trip 60min from PdV centroid; spine_area is Le Marais (the surrounding neighborhood Area).
Strategy at PdV must be trigger_address (23 distinct addresses dominate 6 sub_locations).

Algorithm naturally pulls neighboring Marais POIs under the spine (measured 2026-07-30: Place des Vosges + Musee Carnavalet + Hotel de Sully); their beats are not in expected_stable_beat_ids and extras are never penalized. The gate is an ABSOLUTE hit count (OVERLAP_MIN_HITS in tests/test_tour_golden_pdv.py), not a ratio, so re-keying this fixture cannot move the bar by changing its own denominator. This document is a deep one-square walk (arcade address by address) and the engine builds a multi-POI route, which is why overlap is 4/21 and not near the 90% target — see that file's comment for why closing it is an engine-design question, not a threshold to retune.
